original.evidence: Plans/Models_System.md:9930–9957 says “One receipt is written for every provider attempt” and types requested, policy, effective and provider-wire effort, nullable fields, reset detection, source and reasons. The JSON example shows the transformed effort and provider mapping. Lines 10010–10037 define admission gates, normalized integer factors, weights and ties. The rule is “`total_score = sum(weight * factor_score)`, an integer from 0 to 100000.” The worked example at 10068–10090 yields 75000, 57500 and 55000. The known 450000 estimate fails the 200000 budget, and the unknown estimate remains eligible and visibly unknown as DL-2604 requires.

Plans/Media_Generation_and_Capabilities.md:965–972 and MGAC-066 at 4703 give three BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED variants. The image-only copy requires the backend's own unexpired verified image route, no verified audio or video route and a disabled video, TTS or music capability. The canonical unit says “In every other BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED case a no-verified-route message appears”. Settings verification is offered only for an unverified row that admits the probe. An absent or ineligible row gets the text without a verify action. This applies the same Cursor admission rule as MGAC-061.

Plans/Commands_System.md:329 defines the positional item with optional string name and hint, optional boolean required, and says “readers preserve unknown item keys.” Line 339 follows DL-2604 and says “the GUI authors exactly one argument value”. New Command and Edit at 555 and 569 both expose the 200-character Arguments hint bound to arguments[0].hint. Line 337 specifies lossless editing, including the positional case where “when later items exist, the emptied first item stays as `{}`”. The addendum at 4367 withdraws the richer active schema and the list-editor request.

original.evidence: Plans/GitHub_Integration.md:2089–2130 types compare_origin, its project or application scope, the eight origins and their two-way or three-way operands. Lines 2132–2161 bind graph patches to Contracts_V0. “Its fields are the five joins GI-025 requires.” They type the patch point, concern refs, structural change, affected generation and requester, plus state transitions, rejection and decision/report refs. Lines 2163–2182 require pin identity, path, verification state, commit OID or explicit null, timestamps and command receipt provenance. A pin starts “before the first Actions observation” and a stale generation has an explicit refusal. The shared scope and state references resolve.

Plans/Section15_MVP_Promoted_Features_Spec.md:19278 gives all eleven records a session engine owner and says “they live in memory for that session and are dropped when it ends.” Line 19282 requires “one JSON object (RFC 8259, UTF-8)” with record_type and schema_version 1.0.0. Lines 19284–19298 type each field and transport. TerminalIngestionReceipt has typed stage, count, acceptance and optional chunk refs. TerminalBackpressureState has queue depth, dropped frame count and a closed throttle state. SP-332 separately owns saved scrollback.

Plans/Section15_MVP_Promoted_Features_Spec.md:19278–19284 assigns session-local memory, a closed UTF-8 JSON envelope and explicit export boundaries. “Unknown fields, missing required fields and values outside the types below are refused” and “The user-requested diagnostic bundle of `#SMPFS-076` is the one export these records have.” The eleven rows at 19288–19298 individually name their allowed consumers, including client-to-Server input and a web-only render frame. The starting engine owns TerminalProfileResolution before the session is live.

Plans/Section15_MVP_Promoted_Features_Spec.md:9950–9958 adds tier to the action table. The share row pairs `cmd.browser.share_with_agent` with `guaranteed_everyday`, and `cmd.browser.open_devtools` with `advanced_debug_testing`. Line 9962 says “A command takes the highest level any of its effects reaches”. Lines 9974–9977 assign 50 distinct command spellings, including the named Browser Program exceptions, consistent with DL-2604. The unsupported trace/video command is distinguished from the two catalogued screenshot actions.

Plans/agent-rules-context.md:2430 specifies “get_agent_rules_context(request: &AgentRulesContextRequest) -> AgentRulesContextResult” and “the result is usable if and only if `errors[]` is empty.” With only warnings the caller prepends the assembled block. On error, “`formatted_block_ref` is null, `byte_count` is 0, and the caller must not start the agent run”. This covers missing versus unreadable project rules, stale revisions and strict budget failure for all three callers. The older String signature is explicitly illustrative.
